ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian ساکن (sākin), from Arabic سَاكِن (sākin), from the active participle of the verb سَكَنَ (sakana, “to live, to inhabit”), from the root س ك ن (s-k-n).

Inherited from Prakrit 𑀲𑀺𑀁𑀖𑀸𑀟𑀕 (siṃghāḍaga), from Sanskrit शृङ्गाटक (śṛṅgāṭaka, “water caltrop”). The Sanskrit term seems to be from शृङ्ग (śṛṅga, “horn”), but it is likely to be a back-formation from the Prakrit term rather than a genuine derivation. Note that the Prakrit and Hindi terms have aspirated gh unlike the supposed Sanskrit etymon. Cognate with Bengali সিঙ্গাড়া (śiṅgaṛa, “samosa”)

s.g: Indian Ocean (the ocean separating Africa, southern Asia, Australia and Antarctica)
